questions.question: What should you do when entering a turn?
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning. If you turn too fast, you may slide out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: What kind of helmet gives you the most protection?

options.text: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
A helmet that has survived a previous crash.
A helmet that provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect a motorcycle?

options.text: It usually makes no difference in how the motorcycle handles.
It is usually safe for beginning riders.
It can change how the motorcycle handles.
It is encouraged to help riders practice different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can change how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to the motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: The best thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash is to wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.question: Why should you ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass?

options.text: It helps you see further ahead.
It makes it hard to see past the other vehicle.
It allows the other driver to go faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see further ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see further ahead and makes other drivers more aware of you.

questions.question: How should jackets and pants fit when riding?

options.text: Loose enough for wind to catch the fabric.
Snug enough so they do not flap in the wind.
Tight enough to prevent any movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug enough so they do not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a right turn. Making a right turn here would be unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: What do you need to do as your motorcycle speeds up?
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle goes faster, shift up into higher gears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign means you are near a school. Watch for children and be ready to stop if they are crossing.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider improve their visibility?
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials. Use your headlight at all times. Use your signals and brake light properly. These steps help other drivers see you.

questions.question: Why is your lane position important when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: It has little effect on whether other drivers can see you.
It is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
It cannot protect you from wind from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps other drivers see you. It also helps you see other vehicles and protects you from wind blasts from nearby vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is starting ahead. The road splits into two separate one-way roadways. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.explanation: This sign warns of two-way traffic.

questions.question: What happens if you refuse to take a breath test when an officer asks?

options.text: It is your right and there will be no negative consequences.
It is not a serious offense.

questions.explanation: When you ride on roadways, you agree to take a chemical test if an officer asks. Refusing the test will result in at least one year of license suspension.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you to be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on a vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it both day and night.

questions.question: How can you stay safer when riding at night?

options.text: Night riding is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Only ride at night in the city.

questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night. This makes other drivers more likely to see you.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, what should you do?

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of the lane so the other driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is where drivers are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: Why is riding difficult right when rain starts?

options.text: Other drivers may not react quickly to the rain.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather.

questions.explanation: When rain just starts, the pavement is especially slippery. Oil from vehicles has not yet washed away and mixes with water to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Pre-ride checks only from a mechanic.

questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car. Check your motorcycle carefully before every ride.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Do not matter much since motorcycles are small.
Are very important to warn other drivers of your plans.
Should not be used if no vehicles are nearby.
Are more complex than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to warn other drivers of your plans.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are at greater risk. Use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do. Always use them when turning or changing lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's following distance:

options.text: Should change based on road and weather conditions.
Is not needed in most situations.
Should be short to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should change based on road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Leave more space if your motorcycle needs extra time to stop. Increase your distance on slippery roads, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or in heavy traffic.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, when stopped at an intersection, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: Can clothing reduce injury in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just personal choice.
Yes, but only if the clothing is very loose.
Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing reduces crash injuries. Wear a jacket and pants made of strong material that cover your arms and legs. They should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: People are walking along the road ahead.
Construction workers are on the road.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a pedestrian crossing. Drive carefully in areas where pedestrians may be present.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You do not need to look over your shoulder if you use mirrors.
Mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
You can trust that drivers will respond to your signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head and check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Unlike other substances, alcohol:

options.text: Must be digested before entering the bloodstream.

questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It goes straight into your blood through the stomach and small intestine, quickly affecting your brain.

questions.question: To reduce fatigue while riding, you should:
questions.explanation: Take rest breaks often on long rides to fight fatigue. Caffeine may help at first but can make you very tired when it wears off. Wear warm clothing and use a windshield to protect yourself from wind and rain on long trips.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. Using both brakes together is most effective.
